review.method: Explicit coding-assistant lexical/constituent review of exact N1904 Greek and displayed LSV. Inflection, syntax, repetition and witness differences checked; pending independent peer and reader review. No raw LSV Strong-tag or inferred global lexical assignments.
review.sourceTokenization: Explicit zero-based whitespace tokens including punctuation.

3:1.sourceText: Τὸ λοιπὸν προσεύχεσθε, ἀδελφοί, περὶ ἡμῶν, ἵνα ὁ λόγος τοῦ Κυρίου τρέχῃ καὶ δοξάζηται καθὼς καὶ πρὸς ὑμᾶς,
3:1.targetText: As to the rest, pray, brothers, concerning us, that the word of the LORD may run and may be glorified, as also with you,

groups.note: πρός with the recipients describes the corresponding reception/glorification of the word among/with you; LSV uses with for this contextual relation.

3:2.sourceText: καὶ ἵνα ῥυσθῶμεν ἀπὸ τῶν ἀτόπων καὶ πονηρῶν ἀνθρώπων· οὐ γὰρ πάντων ἡ πίστις.
3:2.targetText: and that we may be delivered from the unreasonable and evil men, for not all [are] of the faith;

groups.note: Greek has not of all [is] the faith, meaning faith does not belong to everyone; LSV recasts this as not all [are] of the faith. The all/faith noun constituent retains the same participants through this possessive-to-membership predicate recast; no isolated nominative article is falsely made the source of of.

unmappedTarget.reason: English copula supplied in a Greek verbless clause; no corresponding finite Greek verb.

3:3.sourceText: Πιστὸς δέ ἐστιν ὁ Κύριος, ὃς στηρίξει ὑμᾶς καὶ φυλάξει ἀπὸ τοῦ πονηροῦ.
3:3.targetText: but faithful is the LORD who will establish you, and will guard [you] from the evil [one];

groups.note: The one Greek ὑμᾶς is the shared object of establish and guard; English repeats that same object in brackets with guard. Both English mentions anchor to this actual shared pronoun.

The substantival genitive adjective τοῦ πονηροῦ is rendered the evil [one]. The whole nominalized adjective supports the English nominalizer one, without inventing a separate Greek person noun or deciding between personal and abstract interpretations.

3:4.sourceText: πεποίθαμεν δὲ ἐν Κυρίῳ ἐφ’ ὑμᾶς, ὅτι ἃ παραγγέλλομεν καὶ ποιεῖτε καὶ ποιήσετε.
3:4.targetText: and we now have confidence in the LORD, that which we command you both do and will do;

groups.note: The perfect πεποίθαμεν denotes the speakers settled confidence; LSV expands the resultant state as we now have confidence. Now is part of that English resultative phrasing, not a separate Greek νῦν token.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek explicitly adds ἐφ’ ὑμᾶς, regarding/toward you, to the confidence statement. LSV has confidence in the LORD and proceeds directly to the that-clause, with no separate regarding-you phrase. The later actual you subject of do is linked to its own finite predicate.

3:5.sourceText: Ὁ δὲ Κύριος κατευθύναι ὑμῶν τὰς καρδίας εἰς τὴν ἀγάπην τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ εἰς τὴν ὑπομονὴν τοῦ Χριστοῦ.
3:5.targetText: and the LORD direct your hearts to the love of God, and to the endurance of the Christ.

groups.note: Greek κατευθύναι is an optative wish that the Lord direct their hearts; LSV uses bare direct for the wish, not a claim that the Greek is an imperative.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

3:6.sourceText: Παραγγέλλομεν δὲ ὑμῖν, ἀδελφοί, ἐν ὀνόματι τοῦ Κυρίου Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ στέλλεσθαι ὑμᾶς ἀπὸ παντὸς ἀδελφοῦ ἀτάκτως περιπατοῦντος καὶ μὴ κατὰ τὴν παράδοσιν ἣν παρελάβετε παρ’ ἡμῶν.
3:6.targetText: And we command you, brothers, in the Name of our Lord Jesus Christ, to withdraw yourselves from every brother walking disorderly, and not after the tradition that you received from us,

groups.note: The Greek accusative subject ὑμᾶς of the withdrawing infinitive is rendered yourselves with the English reflexive/middle withdraw construction. The same recipients are the withdrawing subjects; no third-person reflexive is substituted.

unmappedTarget.reason: Source-witness title difference: LSV our Lord follows additional TR ἡμῶν; N1904 has the Lord title without that possessive in this verse.

3:7.sourceText: αὐτοὶ γὰρ οἴδατε πῶς δεῖ μιμεῖσθαι ἡμᾶς, ὅτι οὐκ ἠτακτήσαμεν ἐν ὑμῖν,
3:7.targetText: for you have known how it is necessary to imitate us, because we did not act disorderly among you;

3:8.sourceText: οὐδὲ δωρεὰν ἄρτον ἐφάγομεν παρά τινος, ἀλλ’ ἐν κόπῳ καὶ μόχθῳ νυκτὸς καὶ ἡμέρας ἐργαζόμενοι πρὸς τὸ μὴ ἐπιβαρῆσαί τινα ὑμῶν·
3:8.targetText: nor did we eat bread of anyone for nothing, but in labor and in travail, working night and day, not to be chargeable to any of you;

groups.note: The one ἐν governs both coordinated labor/travail datives. English repeats in in both limbs; both occurrences stay anchored to the actual shared preposition.

The purpose infinitive πρὸς τὸ ... ἐπιβαρῆσαι means in order not to burden anyone. LSV expresses the same economic relation as not to be chargeable to anyone; the full purpose/burden predicate is kept together through the active-to-predicative recast.

3:9.sourceText: οὐχ ὅτι οὐκ ἔχομεν ἐξουσίαν, ἀλλ’ ἵνα ἑαυτοὺς τύπον δῶμεν ὑμῖν εἰς τὸ μιμεῖσθαι ἡμᾶς.
3:9.targetText: not because we have no authority, but that we might give ourselves to you [as] a pattern, to imitate us;

groups.note: τύπον is a predicative accusative with give ourselves, rendered [as] a pattern. The bracketed as makes that predicate relation explicit in English; the Greek is the pattern noun, not a separate as conjunction.
The articular purpose infinitive εἰς τὸ μιμεῖσθαι is rendered as English to imitate; the whole purpose/infinitive constituent is retained.

3:10.sourceText: καὶ γὰρ ὅτε ἦμεν πρὸς ὑμᾶς, τοῦτο παρηγγέλλομεν ὑμῖν, ὅτι εἴ τις οὐ θέλει ἐργάζεσθαι, μηδὲ ἐσθιέτω.
3:10.targetText: for even when we were with you, this we commanded you, that if anyone is not willing to work, neither let him eat,

3:11.sourceText: ἀκούομεν γάρ τινας περιπατοῦντας ἐν ὑμῖν ἀτάκτως, μηδὲν ἐργαζομένους ἀλλὰ περιεργαζομένους·
3:11.targetText: for we hear of some walking disorderly among you, working nothing, but being busybodies,

3:12.sourceText: τοῖς δὲ τοιούτοις παραγγέλλομεν καὶ παρακαλοῦμεν ἐν Κυρίῳ Ἰησοῦ Χριστῷ ἵνα μετὰ ἡσυχίας ἐργαζόμενοι τὸν ἑαυτῶν ἄρτον ἐσθίωσιν.
3:12.targetText: and such we command and exhort through our Lord Jesus Christ, that working with quietness, they may eat their own bread;

groups.note: The dative substantival adjective τοῖς τοιούτοις identifies the people addressed; English uses the object such with command/exhort, retaining the same people.

N1904 invokes the command/exhortation ἐν Κυρίῳ, in the Lord; LSV through follows TR διά. The contextual relation of the Lord as the authority for the exhortation is retained with the changed preposition reading explicit.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

unmappedTarget.reason: Source-witness title difference: LSV our follows additional TR ἡμῶν; N1904 has no first-person possessive with the Lord title here.

3:13.sourceText: Ὑμεῖς δέ, ἀδελφοί, μὴ ἐγκακήσητε καλοποιοῦντες.
3:13.targetText: and you, brothers, may you not be weary doing well,

3:14.sourceText: εἰ δέ τις οὐχ ὑπακούει τῷ λόγῳ ἡμῶν διὰ τῆς ἐπιστολῆς, τοῦτον σημειοῦσθε, μὴ συναναμίγνυσθαι αὐτῷ, ἵνα ἐντραπῇ·
3:14.targetText: and if anyone does not obey our word through the letter, note this one, and have no company with him, that he may be ashamed,

groups.note: N1904 συναναμίγνυσθαι is an infinitive, not to associate/mix with the person; LSV renders it with the finite command have no company, following TR συναναμίγνυσθε. The association predicate is linked with the grammatical-form difference noted.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

unmappedTarget.reason: Source-witness connective difference: LSV and before have no company follows additional TR καί; N1904 has the following infinitive without that conjunction.

3:15.sourceText: καὶ μὴ ὡς ἐχθρὸν ἡγεῖσθε, ἀλλὰ νουθετεῖτε ὡς ἀδελφόν.
3:15.targetText: and do not count as an enemy, but admonish as a brother;

3:16.sourceText: Αὐτὸς δὲ ὁ Κύριος τῆς εἰρήνης δῴη ὑμῖν τὴν εἰρήνην διὰ παντὸς ἐν παντὶ τρόπῳ. ὁ Κύριος μετὰ πάντων ὑμῶν.
3:16.targetText: and may the LORD of peace Himself always give to you peace in every way; the LORD [is] with you all!

groups.note: The optative δῴη is the wish may give; may expresses the actual Greek verbal mood, not a separate source permission word.
διὰ παντός is the adverbial idiom at all times/always; the preposition and substantival quantifier form one expression.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

unmappedTarget.reason: English copula supplied in a Greek verbless clause; no corresponding finite Greek verb.

3:17.sourceText: Ὁ ἀσπασμὸς τῇ ἐμῇ χειρὶ Παύλου, ὅ ἐστιν σημεῖον ἐν πάσῃ ἐπιστολῇ· οὕτως γράφω.
3:17.targetText: The salutation by the hand of me, Paul, which is a sign in every letter; thus I write.

groups.note: The instrumental dative τῇ ... χειρί is rendered by the hand; the possessive adjective between these source words remains linked separately to of me.
Greek Παύλου is genitive Paul’s in the signed-my-own-hand description; LSV gives Paul as an appositional self-identification after of me. The actual named person is unchanged.

3:18.sourceText: ἡ χάρις τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ μετὰ πάντων ὑμῶν.
3:18.targetText: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ [is] with you all! Amen.

Source-witness ending difference: LSV Amen follows additional TR ἀμήν, absent in N1904.
